correctness.rationale: For the centered counting-measure maximal map on unit-edge K_{m,n}, m>=2 and n>=10^6(m+1)^6, the three ball averages are precisely singleton, the opposite-class star ball, and the global mean. The selected positive linear map T (radius 0 on A; radius 1 on B) has a two-dimensional class-constant singular block whose T*T has trace 1+(mn+1)/(m+1)^2 and determinant (m+1)^(-2), and orthogonal remaining eigenvalues 1 and (m+1)^(-2). Its Perron eigenvector yields c=m/((m+1)^2 Lambda-1)>0 and activates those balls strictly. To prove global optimality, the sum-of-squares upper bound forces every actual nonlinear maximizer to have B mass b=O_m(n^-1/2) and A coordinates near their positive mean, whence all selectors are strictly the same T for the stated very large threshold. This closes a potential gap from merely optimizing one selector; simplicity gives exactly all extremizing moduli, independent signs. Expansion of the quadratic root gives the stated n^-1 coefficient. Analytical inequalities, not finite trials, support all n at the threshold; no claim for smaller n.
